## 🤖 Claude *(22:57:09)*

<details>
<summary>💭 Thinking Process</summary>

Both destructive-PATCH scripts rely on `process.env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`, which was a legacy key disabled back in June 2026. On August 8th, when those scripts ran, the PATCH requests would've hit a 401 error with the message about legacy API keys being disabled, causing PostgREST to reject the writes entirely. The same thing happened with the create POST request — it also failed with a 401, so no `created.id` was ever returned, which is exactly why the /tmp/v4-update-payload.json file never got created in the first place.

So finding #4's claim about destruction is actually refuted: those two curl-based PATCH operations couldn't have written anything because the server had already disabled that key 68 days prior. The code itself is dangerous (no guards, no backups), but no actual destruction happened through those paths. Even if `process.env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` was undefined rather than set to the legacy key, it would still fail the same way — "Bearer undefined" would also return 401. Meanwhile, patch-graph-admin.ts uses a different secret (SB_SECRET_KEY in the new format), but that one's showing as "Unregistered API key" today, suggesting it was revoked or rotated at some point. I can't determine exactly when that happened, so I can't rule out whether it was already dead on August 8th.…

</details>

CONFIRMADO: **O master v4 é mudo e estático — e a prova é muito mais forte do que a do auditor.** Não me contentei com o crest factor: rodei `mpdecimate` nos 22 clipes normalizados que formam o master e **todos os 22 têm exatamente 1 frame único em 210** (`norm_01…norm_22`, `dur=7.000000` cada, 22 × 7,000 = 154,000s exatos). Extraí dois frames do master (t=3s e t=80s) e olhei: são cartelas pretas com moldura ciano, "CENA 01 / 22" e "CENA 12 / 22" — e o texto vem **truncado no meio da palavra** ("EP06 · A SEMAN", "Gancho — As Duas Jaul", "GenOffice (1 Eng · 7 Dias · 0"), defeito extra de `drawtext` que o auditor nem viu. No áudio, `astats` (filtro diferente do `volumedetect` que ele usou) dá **noise floor de −14,42 dB** contra peak −14,04 no v4 (piso de ruído colado no pico = tom contínuo) versus **noise floor −92,43 dB** no v32 (silêncio real entre frases); `silencedetect` a −50 dB encontra **zero** trechos silenciosos em 154s de "narração". E provei o tom: extraí 1s de PCM do `bg_music.wav` e contei **220 cruzamentos por zero = fundamental de 110,0 Hz exatos**, pico absoluto 232/32768 (−43 dB). O `speech_track.wav` tem **um único bucket de histograma** (`histogram_91db: 14784000` — todas as amostras idênticas), silêncio digital puro. Acrescento o agravante que fecha o caso: o próprio `assemble-v4-master.cjs:103` **imprime `áudio=MUDO` cena a cena** durante a execução, e o master foi publicado assim mesmo.

CONFIRMADO (com uma correção de atribuição que não muda o veredito): **o bucket `creative_assets` não existe.** Fiz um teste diferencial que o auditor não fez — sondei cinco nomes de bucket com a chave publishable: `creative_assets` → `NoSuchBucket`, exatamente o **mesmo erro de um nome inventado** (`nope-does-not-exist` → `NoSuchBucket`), enquanto `canvas-assets`, `generated-videos` e `video-studio-assets` respondem `NoSuchKey` (bucket existe, chave não).
